section 8

 

q28

In [ ]:
The analysis identified several strong indicators of diabetes.
HbA1c, fasting glucose, postprandial glucose, BMI, and diabetes
risk score showed the strongest relationships with diabetes diagnosis.

Patients diagnosed with diabetes generally exhibited higher glucose
levels and HbA1c values than non-diabetic individuals. Family
history and hypertension also appeared to be associated with a
higher prevalence of diabetes.

Correlation analysis showed that clinical measurements such as
HbA1c and fasting glucose are highly predictive and should be
considered important features for future predictive models.
Further investigation should focus on feature selection, handling
class imbalance, and evaluating potential data leakage from
derived variables such as diabetes_risk_score
